title: By Friday?
objective: Confirm whether a work deadline includes Friday, then restate the exact cutoff.

scenario.prompt: Your manager writes: ‘Please send the revised rota by Friday.’ You need the exact deadline before promising delivery.

model.clarify: Just to confirm, do you need it before Friday starts, or anytime on Friday?
model.confirm: Understood. I’ll send it no later than 3 p.m. Friday.

language_focus.meaning: By marks the latest acceptable point. On places an event on that day.
form: by + deadline: by Friday; by 3 p.m. Friday
on + day/date: on Friday; on 27 September
language_focus.appropriateness: When ‘by Friday’ lacks an exact hour, clarify the cutoff. Workplaces may interpret the day differently.
language_focus.distinction: ‘Send it by Friday’ allows earlier delivery. ‘Send it on Friday’ places delivery on Friday.

options.feedback: Yes. ‘By’ marks a deadline. Earlier delivery works. The exact Friday cutoff may still need checking.
Not necessarily. ‘On Friday’ places the event that day. ‘By Friday’ also permits earlier delivery.
No. Monday follows the stated deadline. Ask before assuming any extension.

activities.prompt: Which reply finds the missing detail?

options.text: Just to confirm, before Friday starts, or anytime Friday?
options.feedback: Best. It exposes the ambiguity and requests an exact boundary.
This promises a day but never checks the cutoff. The manager may expect it earlier.
This asks about the reason. It does not establish the deadline.

activities.prompt: The manager says, ‘By 3 p.m. Friday.’ Choose the clearest check.

options.text: Understood. No later than 3 p.m. Friday.
options.feedback: Best. It restates the latest acceptable time without changing it.
This reverses the deadline. ‘By 3 p.m.’ means not later than 3 p.m.
Too narrow. A deadline permits earlier completion.

production_task.scenario: A colleague writes: ‘Can you share the figures by Tuesday?’
production_task.instruction: Write one reply. Confirm the cutoff. Then state when you plan to send the figures.
acceptable_examples: Just to confirm, do you need them before Tuesday, or anytime Tuesday? I can send them Monday afternoon.
Do you need the figures by a specific time Tuesday? I plan to send them by noon.
self_check: I used by for the deadline.

retrieval_prompt: Tomorrow, explain the difference: ‘Send it by Friday’ and ‘Send it on Friday.’

visual.title: Deadline window
visual.alt_text: A Monday-to-Friday timeline. A thick line ends at Friday 3 p.m. The line shows any earlier delivery is acceptable. A separate circle on Friday shows that on Friday names the day, not a deadline.
visual.prose: Picture a line running toward Friday. ‘By Friday’ points to the line’s end: finish before or at that boundary. ‘On Friday’ circles Friday itself: the event happens that day. Adding ‘3 p.m.’ makes the boundary visible.
